question: In moist soil, about how deep should maize seed be planted?
choices: Right on the soil surface
About 12-15 cm deep
About 3-5 cm deep
About 10 cm deep

question: When is weed control most important for getting a good maize yield?
choices: During the first few weeks after the maize emerges
Only after the maize has tasseled
Only at harvest time
Weeds never affect maize yield

question: After maize seedlings emerge in a hill, why do farmers thin them to one or two strong plants per stand?
choices: To make the field look tidy
To reduce competition for water, light and nutrients
To attract more birds
So the plants grow shorter

question: In an area with a short rainy season, which type of maize variety is generally the safest choice?
choices: A very late-maturing variety
A variety that needs irrigation
Any variety, maturity does not matter
An early-maturing variety

question: At which stage is maize most sensitive to water shortage (drought stress)?
choices: Just after germination
Around flowering (tasseling and silking)
Only when the grain is fully dry
Maize is not sensitive to drought at any stage

question: Because sorghum seed is small, how deep should it usually be planted?
choices: Shallow, about 2-5 cm deep
Very deep, about 15 cm
Buried about 20 cm below the surface
Left on top of the soil, uncovered

question: Why is it important to thin sorghum to the recommended plant spacing?
choices: Overcrowded plants always yield more
Plant spacing has no effect on sorghum
Too many plants compete and produce small heads
Wider gaps stop the plants from flowering

question: Pearl millet is especially well suited to which kind of growing conditions?
choices: Waterlogged, flooded fields
Cool highland areas with frost
Heavy clay that stays wet all season
Sandy soils in hot, dry, low-rainfall areas

question: Among common cereals grown by smallholders, which is generally best able to give a harvest in the driest, sandiest areas?
choices: Lowland rice
Irrigated wheat
Pearl millet
Sugarcane

question: In lowland rice growing, what does 'transplanting' mean?
choices: Broadcasting dry seed onto flooded soil
Moving young rice seedlings from a nursery into the main field
Harvesting the rice by hand
Draining all the water from the field

question: Why do lowland rice farmers build small earth bunds (ridges) around their fields?
choices: To hold water in the field for the rice crop
To keep all water out of the field
To provide shade for the plants
To mark where to store harvested grain

question: For best results, rice seedlings are usually transplanted while they are still:
choices: Fully mature and flowering
Dry and dead
Young, a few weeks old
Already carrying grain

question: Why is transplanting rice in regular rows and spacing better than scattering seedlings randomly?
choices: It makes weeding much harder
It uses far more seed
Random planting always yields more
It makes weeding easier and gives plants even room to grow

question: When growing cowpea as a sole crop, why is proper plant spacing important?
choices: It gives each plant enough room, light and moisture for good pods
Crowding closer than recommended always doubles the yield
Spacing only matters for cereal crops
Wide random gaps guarantee the best harvest

question: Cowpea is a legume. What benefit does growing it in rotation with cereals like maize often give the soil?
choices: It removes all nutrients from the soil
It helps add nitrogen to the soil for the next crop
It makes the soil permanently barren
It has no effect on the soil

question: How can an early-maturing cowpea variety help a farmer in an area with a short or unreliable rainy season?
choices: It needs continuous flooding to grow
It grows for many years without a harvest
It can produce a crop before the rains end (drought escape)
It can only be grown in the dry season

question: Planting common beans at the recommended spacing rather than throwing seed thickly helps because:
choices: Thick crowding always increases pod yield
Spacing makes no difference to beans
Crowded beans need less weeding
Well-spaced plants get better light and air and compete less

question: What do climbing (pole) bean varieties need that bush bean varieties do not?
choices: Stakes or other support to climb on
No sunlight at all
To be grown underwater
To be planted about 30 cm deep

question: About how deep are common bean seeds usually planted in moist soil?
choices: On the surface, not covered
Around 3-5 cm deep
About 20 cm deep
About 15 cm deep

question: Why do groundnuts grow best in loose, well-drained sandy or sandy-loam soils?
choices: Because they need waterlogged clay to grow
Because they do not form pods underground
So the pegs can enter the soil easily to form pods
Because loose soil stops the plant from flowering

question: Why is even, recommended spacing important when planting groundnuts?
choices: Crowded plants always give bigger nuts
Spacing does not matter for groundnuts
Wide random gaps guarantee more nuts
Good spacing reduces competition and helps pods develop well

question: What is a common sign that a groundnut crop is ready to harvest?
choices: The leaves start to yellow and the pods are well filled
The plants have only just started flowering
The seed has only just germinated
The field is still bright green with no pods

question: How is cassava normally planted by smallholder farmers?
choices: From its flower seeds
From stem cuttings taken from healthy mature plants
From the leaves only
From the tuberous roots planted whole

question: What makes a good cassava planting cutting?
choices: A thin green shoot tip with no buds
Any short piece taken from a diseased plant
A piece of healthy mature stem with several growth buds (nodes)
A single leaf with its stalk

question: When planting cassava cuttings by pushing them into the soil, they should be placed so that:
choices: They lie flat and are buried deep underground
They are pushed in completely upside down
They float on standing water
The buds point upward, with the cutting upright or slanted

question: Roughly how long after planting is cassava usually ready for harvest?
choices: Around 9-12 months or more, depending on the variety
About 2 weeks
About 3-4 weeks
Only a few days after planting

question: Why do many smallholders intercrop maize with a legume such as cowpea or beans?
choices: Legumes kill the maize plants
It can improve soil fertility and give two harvests from one field
It makes both crops fail
Maize cannot grow near any other plant

question: What is one benefit of rotating maize with a different crop family, such as a legume, from season to season?
choices: It guarantees the field will flood
It forces the farmer to buy new land
It helps maintain soil fertility and break cycles that lower yields
It has no benefit over growing maize every year

question: Why is preparing the land before the rains arrive helpful for rain-fed crops?
choices: It delays planting until after the rains have ended
It stops the seeds from ever germinating
It is only useful for irrigated fields
So the field is ready to plant as soon as the rains start

question: What is an advantage of planting maize in rows compared with scattering (broadcasting) the seed?
choices: It makes weeding, spacing and harvesting easier to manage
It always uses much more seed
It prevents the maize from producing cobs
Row planting is only possible with machines
